title: Tatum's card playing, sight and independence at the Three Deuces
summary: Wilson and Hinton recall Tatum's near-blind card handling, his bounce, and how he had waiters set the tables to find the stand.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And he really could see a little bit through his eyes, I used to play cards with him.
Uh huh.
And he used to -- he would put all the cards up to a bright light and he'd put all the cards up there and sort them and --
Yeah, about two inches from his
eyes, he could see what they were.
That's right, that's right.
And even though -- his piano playing was the piano playing of a blind man -- by touch and by ear, the sight was no good to play.
Right.
But he could see two inches from his eye, a deck of cards, and when he would play cards -- do you remember -- the grace with which he could shuffle a deck of cards?
That's right.
Just like a master card dealer. Didn't he?
Sure did.
Just like he could handle a piano, he could handle a deck of cards.
His dexterity was just beautiful. I worked in the Three Deuces with him. Just amazing.
In some ways, he was the most remarkable and phenomenal human being I had ever been around.
Right.
I had never met anyone, in certain ways, that super, special born ability that he had. He was a very unusual person.
That's right -- he had a great mind to prepare for everything.

I rememeber in the Three Deuces in Chicago, which was this little club in the basement, he would come down early and have the waiters set up the tables, because he didn't want anybody to lead him anyplace, and he would let the waiter set up the tables so that he would know the avenue from the stairs to the bandstand without anybody having to lead him.
And, do you remember - he walked with a little bounce?
Yes! Oh, that bounce when he first stood up. Yes sir.
Right.
Yeah, I forgot about that.
Yeah, these are things that I think most people don't remember about Art, that you should experience. So please go on ...
